problem_statement:
fix: don't drop array elements after a subquery in BQ dialect

Fix incorrect parse of a `SELECT [a, b, ...]` in bigquery dialect when the first element in the array is a subquery.

example of the bug this fixes:
```python
>>> sqlglot.transpile("SELECT [(SELECT 1), 2]", read="bigquery", write="bigquery")
['SELECT ARRAY((SELECT 1))']
```

Affects BigQuery and DuckDB, the two generators that use this helper. The new identity tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix; the full unit suite passes.

This was written with Claude, I've read the code and the CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines, I believe this passes muster.

problem_statement:
fix(parser): allow SEARCH + CYCLE and CYCLE TO ... DEFAULT [CLAUDE]

Fixes #8569: in a recursive CTE, SEARCH followed by CYCLE fails to parse, and so does CYCLE with `TO ... DEFAULT`. Oracle and Postgres accept both. Reproduction:

```python
cte = "WITH t(id, mgr) AS (SELECT 1, NULL FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.mgr FROM t r, emp e WHERE r.id = e.mgr)"
sqlglot.parse_one(f"{cte} SEARCH DEPTH FIRST BY id SET ord CYCLE id SET is_cycle TO 'Y' DEFAULT 'N' SELECT * FROM t", read="oracle")
# ParseError: alias does not support CTE
sqlglot.parse_one(f"{cte} CYCLE id SET is_cycle TO 'Y' DEFAULT 'N' SELECT * FROM t", read="oracle")
# ParseError: column does not support CTE
```

Changes:

- `RecursiveWithSearch` gets optional `to` and `default` args, parsed and printed after `SET`.
- `With` gets an optional `cycle` arg for a CYCLE clause that follows a SEARCH clause. A lone clause still goes into `search`.

Tests: `test_oracle.py` gets `test_recursive_cte` with the query from the issue (SEARCH alone, CYCLE alone, both), and `test_postgres.py` two more identities. Both methods fail on main and pass here. Each new query also runs on Oracle Database Free 23 and PostgreSQL 17. `make style`, `make test` and `make testc` pass.

Column lists (`CYCLE a, b ...`) still do not parse; that changes the shape of `this`, so I left it out.

I drafted this with Claude Opus 5.5, read the diff line by line and can answer for every change.

problem_statement:
Fix `ui.scene` objects created before the scene is mounted

### Motivation

Since the modular object system in 3.16 (#6085), every `Object3D` sends its own `create` call as soon as it is constructed. If the scene component is not mounted yet when that message arrives (e.g. inside an inactive `ui.tab_panel`), the client finds no element and drops the call. When the scene mounts later, the first `init` did not re-send anything, so the objects never appeared. Fixes #6379.

### Implementation

`Scene.run_method` now returns a `NullResponse` until the first `init` has arrived, and `_handle_init` sends the full object state on every `init` (not only on a remount). This restores the 3.15 contract: the client receives all objects on `init`, nothing before. Object state changed before `init` (position, material, texture URL, point-cloud points, ...) is covered by the existing `_resend`, since all setters store their state on the Python object.

Trade-off: in the common case (scene visible at build time) the objects now arrive one round trip later than in 3.16/3.17, because they are no longer queued client-side but sent after `init`. This is the same timing as in 3.15.

problem_statement:
Fix duplicated tab sharing nested tab storage values with the original tab

### Motivation

A duplicated browser tab inherits `app.storage.tab` from the tab it was duplicated from. Nested lists and dicts were not copied but shared, so a change in one tab showed up in the other:

```python
from nicegui import app, ui


@ui.page('/')
async def page():
    await ui.context.client.connected()
    app.storage.tab.setdefault('items', [])
    ui.button('Add', on_click=lambda: app.storage.tab['items'].append(1))
    ui.label().bind_text_from(app.storage.tab, 'items', str)


ui.run()
```

1. Open `/` and click "Add". The label shows `[1]`.
2. Duplicate the browser tab and click "Add" in the duplicate. It shows `[1, 1]`.
3. Switch back to the original tab. It shows `[1, 1]` too, although it should still show `[1]`.

Found while reviewing #6332. Scalar values were not affected.

### Implementation

`Storage._create_tab_storage` filled the new storage with `update(old_storage)`. An `ObservableDict` takes over nested observable collections as the very same objects and only registers itself as another observer, so both tabs held the same list.

The old tab's data is now converted into plain dicts, lists and sets first (`_copy_collections`), and the new storage wraps them into observables of its own. `copy.deepcopy` would not be enough: it separates the values, but the copies keep the original as parent, so the original tab would still be notified about changes in the duplicate.

Values that are not collections are still shared by reference. Tab storage may hold arbitrary objects, which cannot be copied in general.

A `User` test duplicates a tab with a nested list and checks that a change in the duplicate neither reaches the original nor notifies it. With the fix, the example above shows `[1]` in the original tab after the click in the duplicate (checked in Chromium). [※](https://zauberzeug.github.io/colophon/#m=claude-fable-5-1&t=Found%20during%20the%20review%20of%20%236332%3B%20fix%2C%20test%20and%20text%20by%20the%20model%2C%20repro%20run%20in%20a%20real%20browser.&d=2026-10-03&a=claude-code "claude-fable-5-1: Found during the review of #6332; fix, test and text by the model, repro run in a real browser.")

+def _copy_collections(value: Any) -> Any:
+    """Copy nested dicts, lists and sets into plain ones, so that the copy shares none of them with the original."""
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return {key: _copy_collections(item) for key, item in value.items()}
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return [_copy_collections(item) for item in value]
+    if isinstance(value, set):
+        return set(value)

problem_statement:
Fix `show_envvar` output for a sequence or an empty `envvar`

This PR fixes some awkward rendering in the `Error: Invalid value for '--units' (env var: xxxxx)` error message's hint for special cases of environment variables:

| Parameter value | Hint before | Hint after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `envvar=None` | Nothing | Nothing |
| `envvar=""` | `(env var: '')` | Nothing |
| `envvar=[]` | `(env var: '[]')` | Nothing |
| `envvar=["WEATHER_UNITS", "UNITS"]` | `(env var: '['WEATHER_UNITS', 'UNITS']')` | `(env var: 'WEATHER_UNITS', 'UNITS')` |

Also fixes the rendering of help screen:
| Parameter value | Help screen before | Help screen after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `envvar=None` | Nothing | Nothing |
| `envvar=""` | `[env var: ]` | Nothing |
| `envvar=[]` | `[env var: ]` | Nothing |
